body: the box of matches and hand torch smell sharply of bleach. mud outlines between them show that a third object was removed.
title: Box of matches beside the spare mark

body:
Laundry receipt: coveralls from the second circle carried orange pollen from the test rows. The clerk noted numb fingers after handling the bag.

The pollen would not wash out, even after the third rinse.
title: Clothes bag from the test rows

body:
Meal receipt back: six lunches went to the greenhouse crew at the third circle. Two were untouched; beside them someone wrote, "metal taste after noon spray."

The greenhouse tomatoes had curled by evening.
title: Lunch stop for the field crew

body:
Photograph note: the fourth circle shows where three field cars were hosed down. Pale foam ran toward the ditch and the grass along it was dying in a clean strip.

The foam smelled like the spray tanks on the trial plots.
title: Cars rinsed behind the garage

body:
Pocket ledger: gas at this circle was charged to the orchard rig. The return mileage exceeds the marked spray route by forty miles.

The rig's tank still held mix, and the hoses were crusted with yellow residue.
title: Fuel for the orchard rig

body:
Torn note under the clothes label: bag the trial coveralls separately and leave them off the laundry invoice. My wrists blistered while tying the second bag.

The cloth was stiff with dried spray.
title: Coveralls kept off the invoice

body:
Receipt from the marked restaurant: lunches for the crop crew, plus soap and bottled water. A handwritten line says the tap smelled sharp, like the spray mix, before closing.

The crew's hands were raw and cracked.
title: Field lunches at the restaurant

body:
Farm-program mileage page: four cars left for the plots, three returned for washing. The blank driver line sits beside a note about seed-treatment samples on the back seat.

The fourth car was never rinsed.
title: Fleet note with one car missing

body:
Garage receipt at the car label: rinse three crop-study vehicles and keep the fourth outside. The fourth plate is the only one with treated-seed dust still in the trunk.

The rinse bill itself was small and ordinary.
title: Car label beside a field rinse bill

body:
Notebook line at the final circle: one trial car returned late from the plots. Its seats were dusted white with treatment powder and its mileage page had been removed.

The powder came off on my sleeve and stung.
title: Final circle, the last trial car
